literal: Whenever studied, a book's delight is like, whenever associated with, the friendship of those possessing good character.
translation: Just as a great book yields deeper delight every time it is read, so does the friendship of those with noble character grow sweeter the more one associates with them.
modern: நூல்களைப் படிக்கப் படிக்க அவற்றின் நயம் மிகுவது போல, நற்பண்பு உடையவர்களோடு பழகப் பழக அவர்களுடைய நட்பு இன்பம் தரும்.
explanation: This couplet compares the friendship of virtuous people to the reading of great books. A good book does not reveal all its beauty and wisdom on the first reading; instead, every time we re-read it, we discover new depths of meaning and delight. Similarly, the friendship of those with noble character does not grow stale; rather, the more we associate with them, the more we appreciate their goodness and find joy in their company. The poet beautifully uses the parallel of intellectual discovery to describe the emotional and moral growth found in true friendship.
